thread:
sofie: heads-up — we had a small P99 spike on hosted/nyc earlier. Primary model pool hit saturation and requests started queuing. thought: instead of queuing, should we auto-route to compatible quantized variant in-region by default? quick sanity check before i write a proposal. :thinking:

daniel: +1 from me. key question: who wins — tenant quota enforcement or capacity-based fallback? if a tenant is over quota should we still permit fallback (and bill them more) or respect quota first?

katie: UX note: if we do auto-fallback we need the console to show when a request was served by a fallback variant and why (reason code: MODEL_SATURATED). A small banner + per-route timeline + sample request link would help SRE debugging.

praveen: sketch of API surface i had in mind: add a top-level `fallback_policy` field on route config. example: ```json
{
  "fallback_policy": {
    "mode": "capacity_fallback",
    "enabled": true,
    "variants": ["redwood/v1-4bit","redwood/v1-8bit-cpu"],
    "region_preference": ["same_region","nearest_region"],
    "max_latency_ms": 900,
    "respect_tenant_quota": true
  }
}
```
This keeps it explicit and pluggable for rollouts.

mira: telemetry checklist: emit `routing.fallback.count`, `routing.fallback.latency_delta_ms`, `routing.fallback.quality_flag` (bool if fallback variant triggered evaluation regression), and a `fallback.reason` tag. we should also emit `route.active_variant` on per-request traces. link to perf dashboard: https://console/internal/dashboards/fallbacks (placeholder).

sofie: good. also think about soft-circuit: if fallback rate for a route > X% for Y mins, auto-scale primary pool or temporarily bump priority. otherwise too many fallbacks masks an underlying scaling bug.

daniel: ops consideration: prefer same_region fallback to avoid egress and consistent latency. but if same_region variants are out, nearest_region is next. we should make `region_preference` part of policy as praveen suggested.

katie: rollout/telemetry UX: provide a little toggle in route rollouts to "simulate fallback" so product teams can see the impact without actually saturating. fake events show up in console timeline and can be filtered. :white_check_mark:

praveen: implementation note: runtime should check capacity signals from the scheduler (available_slots, estimated_qps) and evaluate fallback_policy synchronously before queuing. if `respect_tenant_quota=false` then fallback shouldn't check tenant token quota; else fallback respects remaining tokens. algorithm: prefer variant with minimal expected latency increase and within `max_latency_ms`.

mira: add an eval hook: whenever a route flips to fallback we should sample N responses for automatic evals against the golden set and surface regressions as alerts if quality drops > threshold. map samples back to request ids.

capacity-bot: [system] capacity-alert: primary model pool `redwood/v1` in region `nyc` reported 94% utilization over 5m at 2123456700. Auto-fallback candidates: `redwood/v1-4bit` (est +60ms), `redwood/v1-8bit-cpu` (est +240ms).

sofie: next steps: praveen will draft the API change + migration plan, mira will spec telemetry fields, katie will mock console UI for the toggle + timeline, daniel + infra will review scheduler hooks. i'll put a short RFC doc in the eng-platform repo by EOD. thanks all. :rocket:
